name: Bodyweight Reverse Lunge
summary: A single-leg dominant lunge that steps backward, which is usually easier on the knees and balance than a forward lunge.
setup: Stand tall with feet hip width apart, hands on your hips or in front of you.
Brace your abs and look straight ahead.
Hold a wall or chair back lightly if you need balance.
execution: Step one foot back about a long stride and land on the ball of the foot.
Lower straight down until both knees are bent to about 90 degrees, with the back knee just above the floor.
Keep your torso upright and the front heel flat.
Push through the front foot to return to standing, then repeat on the other side or finish the set on one leg.
mistakes: Front knee collapsing inward: push it out in line with the middle toes.
Taking too short a step so the front knee travels far forward: step back farther.
Leaning forward at the waist: keep the chest up and the abs braced.
Bouncing off the back knee: lower under control and touch lightly or stop just above the floor.
